2025.TA10.1: The Toronto Atmospheric Fund board will approve its 2024 audited financials and move extra funds into a reserve. This is routine finance work. No policy change is proposed.
2025.TA10.10: The board will privately review the CEO's performance and pay in a closed meeting, since it involves personal information. No policy change is proposed.
2025.TA10.2: The CEO will update the board on the fund's work, staff, and programs. The board just needs to receive the report. No policy change is proposed.
2025.TA10.3: The board will approve the written record of its Investment Committee's March 20 meeting. This is routine paperwork. No policy change is proposed.
2025.TA10.4: The board will approve the written record of its Direct Investment Committee's April 1 meeting. This is routine paperwork. No policy change is proposed.
2025.TA10.5: The board will vote on lending up to $4.5 million in short-term funding to a company building fast chargers for electric vehicles across Ontario. The goal is to speed up installations.
2025.TA10.6: The board will vote on changing its loan program for energy-efficient building upgrades, to fix tax problems and fit current market conditions. It also clarifies the committee's authority over each loan.
2025.TA10.7: The board will approve the written record of its Grants and Programs Committee's April 3 meeting. This is routine paperwork. No policy change is proposed.
2025.TA10.8: The board will vote on approving two grants worth $354,750 for climate projects, including work to speed up low-carbon construction. Approval would release the funding.
2025.TA10.9: The board will approve the written record of its Human Resources Committee's April 25 meeting. This is routine paperwork. No policy change is proposed.
2025.TA11.1: The CEO will update the board on the fund's work, staff, and programs. The board just needs to receive the report. No policy change is proposed.
2025.TA11.10: City Council adopted the Mayor's economic action plan responding to United States tariffs. The board just needs to receive the update and consider matching its policies where it makes sense.
2025.TA11.11: City Council adopted an economic plan responding to United States tariffs. The board just needs to receive the update and consider matching its policies where it makes sense.
2025.TA11.2: The board will receive the fund's 2024 Impact Report, which summarizes its climate results. This is for information only. No policy change is proposed.
2025.TA11.3: The board will approve the written record of its Investment Committee's June 3 meeting. This is routine paperwork. No policy change is proposed.
2025.TA11.4: The board will approve the written record of its Direct Investment Committee's June 24 meeting. This is routine paperwork. No policy change is proposed.
2025.TA11.5: The board will vote on guaranteeing a bank loan of up to $3.5 million to a company building prefabricated wood homes. The fund would repay the bank if the company defaults.
2025.TA11.6: The board will approve the written record of its Grants and Programs Committee's June 26 meeting. This is routine paperwork. No policy change is proposed.
2025.TA11.7: The board will vote on approving three grants worth $266,650 for climate projects, including shifting $100,000 between budgets to cover them. Approval would release the funding.
2025.TA11.8: The board will receive the fund's unaudited financial results for January to March 2025. This is for information only. No policy change is proposed.
2025.TA11.9: The board will review the CEO's annual performance and decide on pay, based on private recommendations from its Human Resources Committee. No policy change is proposed.
2025.TA12.1: The board will receive early findings from a study it funded on building AI data centres sustainably around Toronto and Hamilton while keeping power stable. This is for information only.
2025.TA12.10: The board will approve the written record of its Grants and Programs Committee's October 30 meeting. This is routine paperwork. No policy change is proposed.
2025.TA12.11: The board will vote on approving five grants worth $848,077 and rejecting others, based on staff recommendations. Approval would release funding for the chosen climate projects.
2025.TA12.12: The board will adopt its 2026 meeting schedule, set to avoid clashes with City Council dates and culturally or religiously important days. No policy change is proposed.
2025.TA12.13: The board will revisit its earlier decision on the $3.5 million loan guarantee for a wood-homes company and replace it with updated terms from June 2025. No new project is proposed.
2025.TA12.14: The board will vote on changing its Human Resources Committee rules so the committee no longer needs a councillor, and is made up of three board members including the chair.
2025.TA12.2: City Council appointed Jehad Aliweiwi and Elizabeth McCallion to the board for October 2025 to October 2029, replacing two members, and reappointed Jean Olemou. The board just notes the appointments.
2025.TA12.3: The CEO will update the board on the fund's work, staff, and programs. The board just needs to receive the report. No policy change is proposed.
2025.TA12.4: The board will vote on naming Jehad Aliweiwi as treasurer, the board member who oversees the fund's finances. No policy change is proposed.
2025.TA12.5: The board will vote on appointing two board members to its Audit Committee and one to its Human Resources Committee. No policy change is proposed.
2025.TA12.6: The board will receive the fund's unaudited financial results for the second and third quarters of 2025. This is for information only. No policy change is proposed.
2025.TA12.7: The board will vote on its 2026 operating budget. The balanced budget is funded by investment returns and outside money, costing the City nothing. Approval sets the 2026 spending plan.
2025.TA12.8: The board will approve the written record of its Investment Committee's September 25 meeting. This is routine paperwork. No policy change is proposed.
2025.TA12.9: The board will approve the written record of its Direct Investment Committee's October 28 meeting. This is routine paperwork. No policy change is proposed.
2025.TA9.1: The CEO will update the board on the fund's work, staff, and programs. The board just needs to receive the report. No policy change is proposed.
2025.TA9.10: The board will approve the written record of its Direct Investment Committee's January 23 meeting. This is routine paperwork. No policy change is proposed.
2025.TA9.11: City Council adopted a framework for how the City responds to demonstrations. The board just needs to receive it for information. No new decision is requested.
2025.TA9.12: The board will vote on appointing Councillor Dianne Saxe to its Investment Committee. No policy change is proposed.
2025.TA9.2: The CEO of Peak Power, a company the fund invested in back in 2021, will update the board on its progress. This is for information only. No policy change is proposed.
2025.TA9.3: The board will receive the fund's 2024 Annual Report, showing what it achieved against its 2024 plan. This is for information only. No policy change is proposed.
2025.TA9.4: The board will vote on its 2025 Annual Plan, which sets climate work in four areas: building upgrades, electric vehicles, net-zero new buildings, and clean electricity. Approval sets the year's priorities.
2025.TA9.5: The board will vote on appointing Councillor Dianne Saxe as vice chair of the board. No policy change is proposed.
2025.TA9.6: The board will receive the fund's unaudited financial results for the year ending December 31, 2024. This is for information only. No policy change is proposed.
2025.TA9.7: The board will approve the written record of its Grants and Programs Committee's January 30 meeting. This is routine paperwork. No policy change is proposed.
2025.TA9.8: The board will vote on approving $733,162 for its 2025 programs, including $56,250 to grow electric vehicle programs. Approval releases the program funding for the year.
2025.TA9.9: The board will approve the written record of its Investment Committee's December 12, 2024 meeting. This is routine paperwork. No policy change is proposed.
2025.TE19.1: Council will vote on road changes for the Port Lands flood protection project: making parts of Cherry and Commissioners public roads, extending a Villiers Street closure, and renaming New Cherry Street.
2025.TE19.10: Council will vote on replacing 31 rental townhouses at 90 Eastdale and 2 Secord with a 40-storey building and 35 replacement rentals. Current tenants could return at similar rents.
2025.TE19.11: Council will vote on refusing a 48-storey building with 574 homes at 506-516 Church Street. Staff say it is too big for the area's rules, which protect a heritage building there.
2025.TE19.12: Council will vote on changes to the heritage buildings at 508 and 510 Church Street, home of Crews and Tangos. Approval allows partial demolition while keeping parts of the 1850s-era buildings.
2025.TE19.13: Council will vote on adding five early-1900s apartment buildings on Bloor Street West to the City's Heritage Register. Listing recognizes their history but does not ban future changes.
2025.TE19.14: Council will vote on making Kensington Market a Heritage Conservation District with a plan guiding future changes. New work there would follow heritage guidelines to protect its character.
2025.TE19.15: Council will vote on adding the 1911 Royal George Apartments at 84 Maitland Street to the Heritage Register. Listing recognizes its history but does not ban future changes.
2025.TE19.16: Council will decide whether to allow demolishing houses at 60-68 Soudan Avenue to create a public park tied to a future development. Staff recommend refusing the demolitions.
2025.TE19.17: Council will decide on a rejected application for a sidewalk cafe with a deck at 744 St. Clair Avenue West. It can deny the application or overrule staff and approve it.
2025.TE19.18: The committee will add or remove local business representatives on the boards of three business improvement areas: Historic Queen East, Rosedale Main Street, and St. Clair Gardens.
2025.TE19.19: Council will vote on letting the owners of 1141 Bloor Street West and 980 Dufferin Street build a public tunnel under Bloor Street West to Dufferin station.
2025.TE19.2: Council will vote on an 18-storey building with 175 rental homes, including 6 affordable ones, at 450 Dufferin Street. Approval changes the rules to allow the taller building.
2025.TE19.20: The owners of 495-517 Wellington Street West are appealing for permission to install a large lighted sign on public land, which city rules do not allow. Staff recommend refusing the sign.
2025.TE19.21: Council will vote on closing a laneway near Bloor Street West and Dovercourt Road for 18 months as a construction area for an 11-storey building at 990 Bloor Street West.
2025.TE19.22: Council will vote on keeping traffic and bike lanes on Bloor Street West near Dufferin Street closed longer while tunnel work to Dufferin station finishes.
2025.TE19.23: Council will vote on closing the sidewalk and curb lane on Adelaide Street West for four years to build a 47-storey condo. Pedestrians would use a walkway.
2025.TE19.24: Council will vote on closing part of the sidewalk and parking lane on Spadina Avenue and part of Cameron Street for four years to build a 15-storey hotel.
2025.TE19.25: Council will vote on keeping the sidewalk and curb lane on Avenue Road closed longer while a 20-storey condo is finished. The developer cites labour and delivery delays.
2025.TE19.26: Council will vote on closing the sidewalk and curb lane on St. Joseph Street for 58 months to build a 40-storey seniors' residence and condo at 95 St. Joseph Street.
2025.TE19.27: Council will vote on keeping a lane and sidewalk on Maitland Street closed longer while a 40-storey building at 20-26 Maitland Street is finished. The developer needs more time than approved.
2025.TE19.28: Council will get an update on Ontario Line subway construction: early works, the four main construction packages, and issues at Pape and Exhibition stations. The line should be done by 2031.
2025.TE19.29: Council will vote on marking parts of the private roads at 1603 Bathurst Street as official fire routes, meaning no parking or blocking so fire trucks can always get through.
2025.TE19.3: Council will vote on a 44-storey building at 70-86 Lynn Williams Street with 520 rentals, 13 affordable, plus a public daycare and park. Zoning must change to allow it.
2025.TE19.30: Council will vote on adding or removing on-street accessible parking spaces at the locations listed in the January 2025 report. These are routine monthly changes. No wider policy change is proposed.
2025.TE19.31: Council will vote on adding one on-street accessible parking space for people with disabilities. Because the TTC runs transit on this street, full council must approve it rather than a committee.
2025.TE19.32: Council will get a traffic report on the Ontario Place redevelopment, including the Therme spa and new Science Centre. Lake Shore traffic could rise 23 to 40 percent at busy times.
2025.TE19.33: Council will vote on allowing a wheelchair ramp and steps onto the sidewalk at 67 Adelaide Street East, where a drop-in is becoming a shelter for Indigenous men run by Na-Me-Res.
2025.TE19.34: Council will vote on adding traffic lights at Yonge Street and Delisle Avenue, required for a nearby development, and removing a nearby left-turn ban. Staff say the lights are warranted.
2025.TE19.35: Council will vote on installing nine speed humps on Galbraith Avenue between Victoria Park Avenue and Westview Boulevard to slow traffic. Staff say the street meets the City's traffic-calming criteria.
2025.TE19.36: The committee will appoint Roger Beharry Lall to the Ralph Thornton Community Centre's board for a two-year term, replacing James Topham who resigned. No policy change is proposed.
2025.TE19.37: Council will revisit its earlier decision on the construction area at 316-336 Campbell Avenue and update the laneway closure dates to match the builder's new schedule. No new project is proposed.
2025.TE19.38: Council will vote on a temporary stop sign where the Don Valley Parkway off-ramp meets Bayview Avenue. Bridge work closed the normal merge lane. The sign stays until the lane reopens.
2025.TE19.39: Council will vote on making permanent the school crossing guard at Highbourne Road and College View Avenue near Oriole Park Jr. Public School. Feedback from the school community has been positive.
2025.TE19.4: Council will vote on an 11-storey addition to the care home at 55 Belmont Street, adding 168 long-term care beds and 30 assisted living units plus a bigger parkette.
2025.TE19.40: Council will vote on adding about 20 overnight permit parking spaces on Shuter Street between Parliament and Sumach streets. The change fixes inconsistent parking rules along the street.
2025.TE19.41: Council will vote on adding four speed humps on Woodycrest Avenue between Sammon and Mortimer avenues to slow traffic. Residents voted in favour of the humps.
2025.TE19.42: Council will confirm Jason Ash as the 2025 Agnes Macphail Award recipient. The award honours an outstanding East York volunteer, and the selection committee chose him unanimously.
2025.TE19.43: Council will remove an outdated by-law entry for an accessible loading zone on Dovercourt Road that was physically removed before 2009. No signs or parking spaces change.
2025.TE19.44: Council will vote on ending alternate-side parking on Cloverlawn Avenue and keeping parking on the south side. More than 70 percent of surveyed residents supported the change.
2025.TE19.45: Council will vote on stop signs both ways at Denison Avenue and Carr Street, plus a better crosswalk, to make the west entrance of Randy Padmore Park safer.
2025.TE19.46: Council will vote on speed humps on Niagara Street between King Street West and Adelaide Street West to slow traffic near Niagara Public School. This responds to safety concerns from residents.
2025.TE19.47: Council will vote on banning stopping on part of Shaw Street near Argyle Street and changing parking hours. Poor sight lines have made it unsafe for drivers and cyclists.
2025.TE19.48: Council will revisit its parking decision on Berryman Street, raise the pay-and-display rate to the maximum, and fix the wording before signs are installed. Residents asked for the higher rate.
2025.TE19.49: The committee will formally introduce the by-laws needed to carry out the decisions made at this meeting. No policy change is proposed.
2025.TE19.5: Council will vote on a 64-storey building at 522 University Avenue with 579 homes plus shops and offices, keeping part of the heritage building. Zoning must change to allow it.
